rationale: analyze_expression confirms an explicit, derivative-free relation solvable for L, so equation_type=explicit and integrator=evaluate_explicit. Roles match the pipeline prior exactly: L is the determined output; N, V, D are the three independent sampling axes (diminishing-returns power laws + log-vocabulary tokenizer-compression saturation); all remaining symbols are fixed parameters with no integration dummies. Ranges follow physical magnitudes: N 0.1-50 B params, V 10-256 k vocab, D 10-1000 B tokens, all log-spaced across their 1-3 decade spans (8x8x8=512-point grid). Parameter values (E0=0.5 floor, unit amplitudes, exponents ~0.3) come from auto_balance, which rescaled the interaction amplitudes G,H,J,K so every additive term reaches >=5*sigma at sigma=0.02; converged with no weak terms. The NEW triple-interaction term K/(N^alpha*V^beta*D^gamma*(1+kappa*log V)^nu) peaks at 83x sigma in the small-scale corner, so it is well excited and the benchmark cannot be fit by the parent equation. K was set to 10.35 (mildly above the soft 0.01-5.0 hint) to satisfy the RMS visibility criterion; nu=1.0 is within its 0.2-3.0 hint.

scenario_text: A dense language model is trained with a fixed tokenizer-training procedure and corpus family. N is non-embedding parameter count in billions, V is tokenizer vocabulary size in thousands, D is effective training tokens in billions, and L is unigram-normalized validation loss. This is one concrete training configuration. Literature anchor: the vocabulary scaling law of Tao et al. (2024). During evolution, retain diminishing returns from scale and a meaningful vocabulary mechanism; refinements may involve tokenizer efficiency or vocabulary-capacity interaction, not arbitrary terms.
